documents.abstract: The reactions of cytidine with 22 different 2-O-acyloxyisobutyril chlorides lead to the isolation of the corresponding 2,2'-anhydro-1-(3'-O-acyl-beta-d-arabinofuranosyl)cytosine hydrochlorides 9. These compounds, which all show cytotoxicity against HeLa cells in tissue culture, have been examined for antiviral and antileukemic activity. Activity against DNA viruses (vaccinia and Herpes) in tissue culture is maximal in compounds containing acyl groups with 8--12 carbon atoms. Activity against L1210 leukemia in mice varies markedly according to the length of the acyl groups, and high activities were observed in the case of long-chain (C16--C22) esters. The reaction between cytidine and O-acetylsalicyloyl chloride provides an alternate route for the synthesis of 3'-O-Ac cycloC hydrochloride.
documents.authors: Hamamura EK, Prystasz M, Verheyden JP, Moffatt JG.
documents.title: Reactions of 2-acyloxyisobutyryl halides with nucleosides. 6. Synthesis and biological evaluation of some 3'-acyl derivatives of 2,2'-anhydro-1-(beta-D-arabinofuranosyl)cytosine hydrochloride.
